ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square ABCD, the side BC is rotated counterclockwise around point B to $BC'$, and $CC'$, $DC'$ are connected. If $\angle CC'D=90^\circ$ and $C'D=2$, what is the length of the line segment BC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, take point O as the midpoint of segment CC$^{\prime}$ and connect BO. \\
According to the condition, BC = BC$^{\prime}$ \\
$\therefore$BO$\perp$CC$^{\prime}$ \\
$\therefore$$\angle$BOC = $90^\circ$ \\
In square ABCD, \\
BC = CD, $\angle$BCD = $90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$$\angle$OCB + $\angle$C$^{\prime}$CD = $90^\circ$ \\
Also, since $\angle$CC$^{\prime}$D = $90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$$\angle$C$^{\prime}$DC + $\angle$C$^{\prime}$CD = $90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore$$\angle$OCB = $\angle$C$^{\prime}$DC \\
In Rt$\triangle$OBC and Rt$\triangle$C$^{\prime}$CD, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle OCB = \angle C^{\prime}DC \\ \angle BOC = \angle CC^{\prime}D \\ BC = CD \end{array}\right.$ \\
$\therefore$Rt$\triangle$OBC$\cong$ Rt$\triangle$C$^{\prime}$CD (AAS) \\
$\therefore$OC = C$^{\prime}$D = 2 \\
$\therefore$CC$^{\prime}$ = 2 OC = $2 \times 2$ = 4 \\
$\therefore$BO = CC$^{\prime}$ = 4 \\
In Rt$\triangle$BOC, \\
BC = $\sqrt{BO^{2} + OC^{2}}$ = $\sqrt{4^{2} + 2^{2}}$ = $\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, ABCD is a square, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Line segment BC is rotated counterclockwise about point B to obtain the upward-slanting BC', and point C' is located inside the square toward the upper left; the figure also connects CC' and DC', and gives the conditions ∠CC'D=90°, C'D=2. Then reason: Take the midpoint O of CC', and connect BO. Because BC' is obtained by rotating BC about point B, BC'=BC, so triangle BCC' is an isosceles triangle. O is the midpoint of the base CC', so BO is the perpendicular to the base CC', namely BO⊥CC', hence ∠BOC=90°, and OC=OC'. In square ABCD, BC=CD, and ∠BCD=90°. Since O, C, C' are collinear, at point C there is ∠OCB+∠C'CD=90°. Also because ∠CC'D=90°, in right triangle C'CD, ∠C'DC+∠C'CD=90°. Therefore ∠OCB=∠C'DC. Compare right triangle OBC and right triangle C'CD: ∠BOC=∠CC'D=90°, ∠OCB=∠C'DC, and BC=CD, so these two right triangles are congruent. Therefore the corresponding side OC=C'D=2. Because O is the midpoint of CC', CC'=2OC=4. From the corresponding sides of the congruent triangles, it can also be obtained that BO=CC'=4. Thus, in right triangle BOC, BC is the hypotenuse, BC=sqrt(BO^2+OC^2)=sqrt(4^2+2^2)=sqrt20=2sqrt5.
